title: Your giving
tomorrow: a fast nobody requires. why would Amira choose one?

cards: A fundraising page with a scrolling list of donor names, and a little box at checkout: show my name, or give anonymously. Some people click without thinking. Some hover over it for a while.
Give quietly, or where people can see? The Qur'an speaks to that choice directly, and Muslims read it two ways.

teach.b: First, the plan itself. Zakat is the required giving: a set share of wealth above a threshold, owed by those who have it, for the people the Qur'an names: "The alms are only for the poor and the needy," the list begins.
Sadaqah is everything beyond that: any amount, any time. A hadith even counts a smile as charity. Now the debate.
In 2:271 the Qur'an says that giving openly is good, and that hiding it and giving to the poor is better for you. Two readings live inside that verse. View one: give where people can see.

Its best case: giving spreads. A name on the list tells the next person this is normal, and some commentators say the required zakat, especially, can be given openly so others follow. View two: give in secret.

teach.h: HIDDEN: THE LEFT HAND DOESN'T KNOW.
teach.b: Its best case: a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari names, among those God shades on the Last Day, a person who gives so quietly that the left hand doesn't know what the right hand gave.
Secrecy guards the heart from wanting applause.
A neighbor says nearly the same: in the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus says, "let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth." Both views give. They part only on the checkbox.

how: Muslims whose wealth is above the threshold pay zakat, and anyone can give sadaqah at any time; some give openly to encourage others, some in secret.

games.q: the two kinds and the two views — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an says only secret giving counts
2:271: giving openly is good; hiding it and giving to the poor is better for you.
a hadith counts a smile as charity
sadaqah isn't only money: a smile can count.
zakat and sadaqah are two names for the same thing
zakat is required, on wealth above a threshold; sadaqah is any giving beyond it.

games.q: you lean toward giving in secret. a friend asks you to make the best case for the other side, giving where people can see. what's the strongest case?
o: a name on the list can encourage the next person to give.
open giving gets you thanked, and you've earned the thanks.
secret giving is selfish, because it hides a good example.
games.why: that's view one at its best: giving spreads, and some commentators say the required zakat can be given openly so others follow. the other two are weak versions nobody in the debate holds.

practice: Make a small giving plan in three lines. What you'll give regularly, even if it's small. Who it's for.
And whether it goes out with your name or without, and why. Hold the plan in mind for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Your giving: your plan for zakat, the required alms, and sadaqah, the giving beyond it. Open or hidden, it gets given.

orig.note: Arabic: voluntary charity, any size, any time.

carryVoice: Your line: my giving, planned before anyone asks, and kept whether or not anyone sees. Five of ten, given.
